quests.sentence: As a child, she had to be home before dark every single evening without exception.
quests.hint: 'Had to' is the past tense of 'have to' - a past obligation.
quests.explanation: 'Had to be' is the past form of 'have to'. It describes a past obligation or rule that applied when she was a child.

quests.sentence: As a university student, she has to manage her time very carefully to meet all her deadlines.
quests.hint: 'Has to' describes a current obligation.
quests.explanation: 'Has to manage' is the present form of obligation ('have to'). The sentence describes a current necessity.

quests.sentence: As a future parent, she will have to be consistent and patient with young children.
quests.hint: 'As a future parent' refers to a role she doesn't have yet.
quests.explanation: 'Will have to be' is the future form of obligation. 'As a future parent' confirms this is a future scenario.

quests.sentence: Without the shortcut, it could have taken her an entire day to process the data.
quests.hint: 'Could have taken' is a past hypothetical - what might have happened.
quests.explanation: 'Could have taken' is the past modal perfect used for a hypothetical past scenario.

quests.sentence: With this new tool, she can process the entire dataset in under five minutes.
quests.hint: 'Can' describes her current capability with the tool.
quests.explanation: 'Can process' is a present modal expressing a current ability or possibility.

quests.sentence: Future versions of this software will be able to automate the entire process.
quests.hint: 'Future versions' refers to software that doesn't exist yet.
quests.explanation: 'Will be able to automate' is the future form of ability. 'Future versions' confirms this is a prediction.

quests.sentence: She may have left her purse at the checkout when she was packing her bags.
quests.hint: 'May have left' is speculation about a past action.
quests.explanation: 'May have left' is the past modal perfect for speculation. The sentence expresses uncertainty about a past event.

quests.sentence: She may need to call the shop to ask if anyone has handed in a lost purse.
quests.hint: 'May need' expresses a present possibility or consideration.
quests.explanation: 'May need' is a present modal expressing a current uncertain possibility.

quests.sentence: Her bank may issue a replacement card within three to five working days.
quests.hint: 'Within three to five working days' is a future time reference.
quests.explanation: 'May issue' is a future modal expressing a future possibility. The card hasn't been issued yet.

quests.sentence: The critics argued that the film might have been far better with a different ending.
quests.hint: 'Might have been' is a past hypothetical speculation.
quests.explanation: 'Might have been' is the past modal perfect for speculation about a past possibility.

quests.sentence: The sequel might not be as well received as the highly praised original.
quests.hint: 'Might not be' expresses a present uncertainty about the sequel.
quests.explanation: 'Might not be' is a present modal expressing a current uncertain possibility.

quests.sentence: The third film in the series might actually be the best of the three.
quests.hint: 'Might be' expresses a future possibility about a film that hasn't been released.
quests.explanation: 'Might be' is a future modal expressing a future possibility. The third film doesn't exist yet.

quests.sentence: She needn't have bought so much food for the party - half of it went to waste.
quests.hint: 'Needn't have bought' means she did it but it was unnecessary.
quests.explanation: 'Needn't have bought' is the past modal perfect, meaning the action was done but was unnecessary in retrospect.

quests.sentence: She need not worry about catering - the venue provides all food and drink.
quests.hint: 'Need not worry' expresses a present lack of necessity.
quests.explanation: 'Need not worry' is a present modal expressing that a current concern is unnecessary.

quests.sentence: She will not need to cook at all during the entire holiday - everything is included.
quests.hint: 'During the holiday' refers to a future period.
quests.explanation: 'Will not need to cook' is a future modal expressing the absence of a future obligation.

quests.sentence: If she had applied for the position sooner, she would have got the job.
quests.hint: 'Would have got' is the result of a third conditional - a past hypothetical.
quests.explanation: 'Would have got' is the past modal perfect in a third conditional. It describes what would have happened in the past.

quests.sentence: If she applies quickly and puts together a strong application, she would stand a good chance.
quests.hint: 'Would stand' expresses a present conditional possibility.
quests.explanation: 'Would stand' is a present conditional modal. The sentence describes a current hypothetical scenario.

quests.sentence: If she secures this position, she will start in the new role the following month.
quests.hint: 'If she secures' is a future condition, and 'will start' is the future result.
quests.explanation: 'Will start' is the future simple in a first conditional. The securing is a future condition.

quests.sentence: He was able to finish all his homework before dinner for once.
quests.hint: 'Was able to' describes a specific past achievement.
quests.explanation: 'Was able to finish' is the past form of ability used for a specific achievement. It refers to a completed past event.

quests.sentence: He is able to study for three hours without losing concentration now.
quests.hint: 'Now' and 'is able to' signal a present ability.
quests.explanation: 'Is able to study' expresses a current capability. 'Now' confirms this is his present level of ability.

quests.sentence: He will be able to achieve much better results if he keeps up this level of effort.
quests.hint: 'If he keeps up this effort' is a future condition.
quests.explanation: 'Will be able to achieve' is the future form of ability. The condition 'if he keeps up this effort' is future.

quests.sentence: If the weather had been better, we would have spent the whole day at the beach.
quests.hint: 'Would have spent' is the result of a past hypothetical - the weather was not good.
quests.explanation: 'Would have spent' is the past modal perfect in a third conditional. The bad weather is implied (it did happen).

quests.sentence: If the weather is good at weekends, they usually take a walk in the local park.
quests.hint: 'Usually' and 'is good' signal a present recurring pattern.
quests.explanation: 'Take' is the present simple in a zero conditional, describing a current regular habit.

quests.sentence: If the weather forecast improves, they will plan a full day trip to the coast.
quests.hint: 'Will plan' is a future result of a first conditional.
quests.explanation: 'Will plan' is the future simple in a first conditional. The improved forecast is a future condition.

quests.sentence: If she had had more free time, she would have made everything from scratch.
quests.hint: 'Would have made' is the past hypothetical result - she didn't have time.
quests.explanation: 'Would have made' is the past modal perfect in a third conditional. She didn't have enough time (implied).

quests.sentence: If she has time at weekends, she always bakes fresh bread for the whole family.
quests.hint: 'Always' signals a regular present habit triggered by a condition.
quests.explanation: 'Bakes' is the present simple in a zero conditional, describing a current repeated pattern.

quests.sentence: If she takes a proper cooking course, she will improve her skills enormously.
quests.hint: 'Will improve' is a future result of a first conditional.
quests.explanation: 'Will improve' is the future simple in a first conditional. Taking the course is a future possibility.

quests.sentence: She was supposed to have taken her medication twice a day but often forgot.
quests.hint: 'Was supposed to have taken' describes an unfulfilled past obligation.
quests.explanation: 'Was supposed to have taken' is a past modal structure expressing an obligation that was not properly met.

quests.sentence: She is supposed to take the new medication with food twice every day.
quests.hint: 'Is supposed to' describes a current medical instruction.
quests.explanation: 'Is supposed to take' is a present modal structure expressing a current obligation or instruction.

quests.sentence: She will need to follow a different course of medication after her next medical review.
quests.hint: 'After her next medical review' is a future event.
quests.explanation: 'Will need to follow' is a future modal expressing a future obligation. 'After her next review' is future.
